title: ABVX Investment Memo
recommendation: Cautious; price bakes in platform value well beyond the de-risked UC asset.
thesis: Lead-asset (UC) rNPV is $1.4B against a $10.02B market cap - the modeled program covers roughly 14% of current value. ABTECT Phase 3 met its primary endpoint and all key secondaries with high significance [11][12], which supports the UC case, but obefazimod's RA and Crohn's programs remain Phase 2 [15][16]. The rNPV-to-market-cap gap implies the market is pricing substantial value for indications that have not yet reached Phase 3.
variant_view: At $10.02B market cap against a $1.4B lead-asset rNPV, the price implies the market is treating obefazimod as a validated multi-indication platform (RA, Crohn's, possibly HIV) already largely de-risked, not just a single UC approval - coverage is only ~14%. Our evidence supports a narrower conclusion: only UC has reached Phase 3 with positive topline data [11][12][15][16]; RA and Crohn's are still Phase 2, with no Phase 3 data disclosed [regulatory summary]. Even substituting the higher grounded PoS of 0.8 [17][18][19] for the valuation's blended 0.57 lifts rNPV to roughly $2.0B - still under 25% of market cap - so the remaining ~$8B in market value is being ascribed to pipeline optionality that current evidence does not yet support. This resolves via the Crohn's Phase 2 readout and the planned Q4 2026 UC NDA filing: a clean UC filing with no incremental RA/CD data would argue the stock is priced for more than is proven, while positive Crohn's Phase 2 data or an accelerated regulatory pathway disclosure would validate the platform premium.

sections.takeaway: Cautious; price bakes in platform value well beyond the de-risked UC asset.

sections.title: Company & Pipeline Overview
sections.takeaway: Abivax is a clinical-stage biotech whose lead asset, obefazimod, has completed Phase 2b induction/maintenance testing in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis and is advancing into Crohn's disease, positioned on a differentiated miR-124 mechanism; cash position is not established in the evidence provided.
sections.prose: Abivax's lead candidate, obefazimod, upregulates miR-124, a natural regulator of inflammatory response, in immune cells [1-10]. The company positions this mechanism as differentiating obefazimod from other IBD therapies by avoiding broader immunosuppression [15-18]. Obefazimod has completed a Phase 2b induction and 48-week maintenance/open-label extension program in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis [21][24][25], and is in an ongoing Phase 2 trial in moderately to severely active Crohn's disease [22]. The molecule originated as an HIV antiviral targeting Rev, showing antiviral activity and reduced HIV DNA/transcription in Phase 2 HIV studies [11-13]. It was also tested in rheumatoid arthritis, safe and well tolerated at 50 mg [14]. Cash position is not disclosed in the evidence provided.

sections.title: Mechanism of Action
sections.takeaway: Obefazimod's differentiated mechanism—selective miR-124 upregulation to restore immune homeostasis rather than broad immunosuppression—has clinical support across HIV, RA, and UC/Crohn's programs, but efficacy data from the pivotal UC and Crohn's trials are not included in the evidence reviewed.
sections.prose: Obefazimod's proposed mechanism is specific upregulation of miR-124 in immune cells [1][2][3][4][5][6], a microRNA the company and independent literature describe as a natural regulator that restores immune homeostasis [7][8][9][10]. ABVX positions this as differentiating versus other IBD therapies by avoiding broader immunosuppression, though this is a company assertion, not independently validated [11][12][13][14]. Originally an HIV antiviral targeting Rev [15], ABX464 showed antiviral activity in a Phase 2 HIV study [16] and reduced total HIV DNA and per-provirus transcription in a substudy [17], supporting biological activity beyond the IBD indication. A placebo-controlled Phase 2a RA trial found the 50 mg dose safe and well tolerated [18]. A Phase 2b UC dose-ranging trial is completed [22] and a Phase 2 Crohn's trial is recruiting [23], but efficacy results from either are not disclosed in the evidence reviewed. Unrelated nematocidal research on ABX464 analogs implicates a distinct aldo-keto reductase target [19][20][21], underscoring mechanistic uncertainty outside the immune context.

sections.title: Probability of Success
sections.takeaway: We estimate a 50-65% probability of success for obefazimod in UC, anchored on a well-powered, positive Phase 3 maintenance trial with a highly significant primary endpoint [1].
sections.prose: The ABTECT maintenance trial was a large, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (~190-195 patients/arm) [3] that met its primary endpoint of clinical remission at Week 44 for both doses (50.8% and 51.3% vs. 10.4% placebo, p<0.0001) [4], the lowest placebo remission rate reported in this trial category, reducing artifact risk [6]. All key secondary endpoints—endoscopic improvement/remission, HEMI, corticosteroid-free and sustained remission—were met with consistent, highly significant effect sizes [5]. Efficacy held in the more refractory Part 2 population [7]. The endpoint aligns with FDA precedent for UC [10]. Mechanism (miR-124 upregulation) is reproducible across HIV, RA, and UC [2]. Safety was favorable in the pivotal trial with no new signals [8], though earlier RA and HIV Phase 2 data show dose-dependent GI AEs and higher AE rates on drug [9]. No CMC/manufacturing evidence is available, and only one indication has reached Phase 3, capping certainty [11].

sections.title: Regulatory Path
sections.takeaway: Obefazimod's Phase 3 ABTECT program cleared a key maintenance readout on June 29, 2026, but no FDA designation is disclosed and the accelerated-vs-full approval path remains unspecified.
sections.prose:
- Obefazimod (ABX464), UC program: Phase 3 ABTECT maintenance trial Part 2 read out positive topline results on June 29, 2026, in a more refractory population (non-responders to induction or relapsers during Part 1 maintenance) [4][5][6][7][8][9].
- Obefazimod, Phase 2b/UC: completed induction and 48-week open-label extension/maintenance study, with primary endpoint of change from baseline in modified Mayo Score at week 8 [1][2][17].
- ABX464, HIV indication: completed a separate Phase 2 trial in fully controlled HIV-infected patients; not part of the current UC regulatory track [3].
- FDA designations: none disclosed for obefazimod (no fast track, breakthrough, orphan, or PRIME status found in evidence); the only "fast track" references relate to French foreign-investment screening rules, not FDA drug designations [10][11][12][13][14][18][19][20][21][22].
- Company characterizes obefazimod as a "potential first-in-class oral miR-124 enhancer," a scientific descriptor, not a regulatory designation [23][24].
- Open question: whether the Phase 3 ABTECT primary endpoint supports accelerated approval or requires full/standard approval is not addressed in available disclosures [15][16].

sections.title: Commercial Opportunity
sections.takeaway: Illustrative gross peak sales for obefazimod in UC run $1.3-3.0B, but every input is an assumption — there is no public epidemiology or pricing for this pre-commercial asset, so treat this as order-of-magnitude, not a forecast.
sections.prose: Peak sales are built on assumed penetration and pricing, not disclosed guidance: gross peak revenue is estimated at $1.3-3.0B, with a deterministic base case of ~$2.11B gross ($1.68B risk-adjusted) [5][6][7][8]. The epidemiology base (~600,000 prevalent US UC patients) itself derives from applying a published prevalence rate to the US adult population, not a UC-specific market study [1]. The one supportive, evidence-grounded input is probability of success: obefazimod has positive Phase 3 ABTECT maintenance results (Part 1 and Part 2) and an NDA submission targeted for late Q4 2026, consistent with an 80% late-stage PoS [2][3][4]. That PoS is applied in the valuation, not in this range. Given the reliance on assumed addressable fraction, peak penetration, and net price, this range should be read as a sensitivity sketch, not a point forecast.

sections.title: Valuation & Price vs Thesis
sections.takeaway: Deterministic rNPV for the lead asset alone runs ~$1.4B (unadjusted NPV $2.5B at 0.57 probability of success), covering only about 14% of the current $10.02B market cap at $114.79/share — the price implies substantially more than the lead-asset math supports.
sections.prose: The rNPV of $1.4B is order-of-magnitude, not a target, and captures only the lead program; the $10.02B market cap prices the whole company, so the ~14% coverage ratio is not upside/downside math, just a gap flag. Balance sheet is solid: EUR 516.7M cash at 2025-12-31 [1], EUR 477.4M (~$548.9M) actual cash plus EUR 34.2M debt at 2026-03-31 [3][4][5][6], and pro forma cash of EUR 1.1B (~$1.26B) post-offering [11], with guided runway into Q2 2029 [12]. Share count is ~79.3M with modest warrant dilution (277K BSA at EUR16.26, 205K BCE at EUR10.20) [7][8][9][10]. Our read: the market price embeds pipeline/optionality value well beyond the lead-asset rNPV — cash and runway are not the constraint here, valuation assumptions are.

sections.title: Risks
sections.takeaway: The thesis rests almost entirely on a single Phase 3 asset (obefazimod) with no regulatory filing yet disclosed and a French sovereign-screening overhang that is unrelated to any FDA fast-track status.
sections.prose:
- Single-asset concentration: obefazimod is Abivax's lead program, still in Phase 3 (ABTECT) with no disclosed FDA filing or approval timeline beyond the Part 2 topline readout on 2026-06-29 [7][8].
- Regulatory designation confusion risk: 'fast track' references in filings concern French foreign-investment screening thresholds under French economic law, not FDA fast track designation for obefazimod — investors should not conflate the two [9][10][11][12][13].
- Foreign-investment/ownership risk: France's Minister of the Economy authorization regime and 25%/10% voting-threshold screening rules could constrain non-EU investor participation or M&A optionality [9][11][13].
- Balance sheet dependent on financing structure: cash position of EUR 516.7M at 2025-12-31 [1] and EUR 477.4M actual basis at 2026-03-31 [14][15] is paired with EUR 34.2M total debt as of 2026-03-31 [16][17]; capitalization tables reference an 'as adjusted' scenario tied to a royalty certificate transaction, implying the actual-basis figures may not reflect pro forma capital structure.
- Dilution risk: 78,536,412 shares outstanding as of 2025-12-31 [2] is a static count; any future financing tied to the royalty certificate repurchase or capital raises is not quantified in these claims.

sections.title: Catalysts
sections.takeaway: The key catalyst has already read out: positive topline Part 2 results from the Phase 3 ABTECT 44-week maintenance trial in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis were announced June 29, 2026 [7][8]; no further dated readouts are disclosed in the evidence.
sections.prose:
- ABTECT Phase 3 maintenance trial (obefazimod/ABX464): Part 2 topline results positive, announced June 29, 2026, following prior Phase 2b induction/maintenance data [7][8][3][4].
- Regulatory filings: evidence contains no disclosed FDA filing date or decision timeline for obefazimod; references to a "fast track" procedure relate only to French foreign-investment screening rules, not FDA fast track designation [9][10][11][12][13].
- Financing backdrop: cash position of EUR 516.7M at 2025-12-31 [1], updated to EUR 477.4M (~$548.9M) cash/short-term investments and EUR 34.2M (~$39.3M) total debt as of 2026-03-31 per recent 424B5 filings [14][15][16][17]; no additional dated catalysts specified.
